articles.title: Global politics and Nordic central banks in focus
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
The relief following the Fed's interest rate hike
 to safeguard confidence in the inflation target was short-lived, with long-term interest rates rising clearly on Friday. Ten-year government bond yields in most countries are now only a few basis points below last week's peaks. In France, the 10-year yield reached its highest level since 2008, while the spread against Germany widened by 6 basis points to 105 basis points.
The S&P 500 recovered
 despite the rise in interest rates and closed slightly higher (+0.2%). The reversal in oil prices, which erased an earlier increase, probably contributed to the turnaround. Despite Trump's threats of further escalation in the Middle East, oil prices continue to fall this morning. US and European equity futures are pointing higher, while most Asian stock markets are also rising. Japan is closed, so there is no cash trading in US Treasuries during Asian hours, but futures suggest that yields will fall back somewhat when Europe opens.
We can look forward to an exciting week
, especially in the Nordic region, with interest rate announcements from Norges Bank and the Riksbank on Thursday. Politics will also be in focus with the UN meeting in New York and a summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and Donald Trump at the White House on Thursday; many meetings are planned between world leaders during the week 
and an agreement on Greenland is expected to be signed
. According to US Treasury Secretary Bessent, the US and China have started preparatory talks in a positive spirit. In a diplomatic statement, the leaders of Canada, Brazil, the EU and Kenya call on the countries of the world to increase global cooperation.
Opinions on how problematic the rising long-term interest rates
 are divided
, but I am leaning in the more pessimistic direction. It is difficult to see how highly indebted countries will be able to reverse the trend when ever higher interest costs contribute to larger deficits. Sooner or later, the market will force measures that lead to tightening and lower growth. Higher interest rates are already contributing to tightening. So far, the market can be said to be on the side of the optimists. The CDS – which reflects the market's assessment of credit risk – is at moderate and stable levels, while stable or even strong currencies for several countries with high interest rates send the same signal. At the same time, Sweden, which has the EU's lowest 10-year yield, has had a weaker currency and a shift towards safe countries, as during the euro crisis, is not discernible. Neither the central banks nor the market seem particularly worried about growth.
In Germany, the setbacks continue for Chancellor Friedrich Merz. 
 In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, the CDU looks set to fall below the five percent threshold and thus be eliminated from the state parliament, while the far-right AfD will become the largest party. The CDU is also losing big in Berlin, where the left-wing party Die Linke is making the strongest progress and will be the largest party. Despite the increased pressure, Merz is so far rejecting demands to resign.
Nordic key stories
Expectations for Norges Bank are divided
, 
but we are, with great hesitation, sticking to the interest rate being raised by 25 basis points. However, slightly lower inflation suggests that the hike can be postponed. A majority in Bloomberg's survey expect an increase, but almost half believe in an unchanged interest rate – and the undersigned is also leaning towards a later increase. More about Norges Bank 
here.
The Riksbank's interest rate announcement and Monetary Policy Report in focus
.
All analysts believe in an unchanged interest rate on Thursday and the market is only pricing in +4 basis points, but according to our interest rate survey, there are those who believe that the interest rate can be raised now in September. Our forecast that the Riksbank will wait until the labour market turns, before raising interest rates, has faced strong headwinds after interest rate hikes from both the Fed and the ECB, which were also interpreted as hawkish by the market. Perhaps even more important are the very sharp increases in fuel and electricity prices, which will push up inflation significantly in the coming months. The risks to our forecast that the interest rate path signals a clear but moderate probability of an interest rate hike in the coming months are on the upside. Unlike most other central banks, the Riksbank has emphasised that the risks of inflation should be weighed against the risk of unnecessarily harming growth. After a long period of stagnation, household consumption looks set to pick up, but the question is what will happen if households are hit by both high energy prices and higher interest rates in the coming quarters. The Riksbank cannot do anything about an energy-driven rise in inflation and, unlike in many other countries, interest rate hikes will also lead to higher CPI inflation and higher rents and tenant-owner fees. The wage negotiations, which will begin with demands from the LO in October, will hardly be made easier by preventive interest rate hikes. Di's Shadow Executive Board believes that the interest rate may remain unchanged in September, but is increasing its plans for interest rate hikes later on (more 
here
, payment link, Swedish).
Attempts to form a government have begun, 
and on Friday, not unexpectedly, Magdalena Andersson received the first of four attempts to find a government that a majority in the Riksdag can tolerate. The introduction has not been particularly optimistic, with both the Left Party (V) and the Center Party (C) sticking tightly to the red lines from the election campaign. C has even said that V must renounce the requirement to be in the government in order to even start talks. It remains to be seen how much of the proposals are negotiation tactics. Both C and V may ultimately be able to live with a pure Social Democratic government. What political concessions will be required in that case, and how C and V will be able to agree on a budget, are much more difficult questions. Magdalena Andersson will report the results of her soundings on September 28.

articles.title: Global politik och nordiska centralbanker i fokus
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
Glädjen efter Feds räntehöjning 
för att säkra förtroendet för inflationsmålet blev kortvarig, och långräntorna steg tydligt i fredags. Den 10-åriga statsobligationsräntan ligger i de flesta länder i dag några räntepunkter under toppnivåerna från förra veckan. I bl a Frankrike nåddes en ny högstanivå sedan 2008 och räntespreaden mot Tyskland ökade med 6 räntepunkter till 105. S&P 500 återhämtade sig under kvällen trots ränteuppgången och stängde svagt upp (+0,2%). Att oljepriset föll tillbaka och reverserade en tidigare uppgång bidrog sannolikt till vändningen. Trots hot om upptrappning från Trump i Mellanöstern fortsätter oljepriset att falla nu på morgonen och börsterminerna i USA och Europa pekar uppåt samtidigt som de flesta börserna i Asien stiger. Japan håller stängt så det är ingen handel i den amerikanska 10-åringen men terminerna tyder på att räntorna kommer falla tillbaka lite när Europa öppnar.
Vi kan se fram emot en spännande vecka
, framför allt i Norden, med räntebesked från Norges Bank och Riksbanken på torsdag. Politiken hamnar också i fokus med FN-mötet i New York och ett toppmöte mellan Kinas president Xi Jinping och Donald Trump i Vita huset på torsdag; många möten är planerade mellan väldens ledare under veckan 
och ett avtal om Grönland förväntas bli underskrivet
. Enligt USA:s finansminister Bessent har USA och Kina inlett förberedande samtal i positiv anda. Ledarna för Kanada, Brasilien, EU och Kenya uppmanar i ett diplomatiskt utspel världens länder till ökat globalt samarbete.
Åsikterna om hur problematiska de stigande långräntorna går i sär
, där undertecknad lutar åt det mer pessimistiska hållet. Det är svårt att se hur högt skuldsatta länder ska kunna vända utvecklingen när allt högre räntekostnader bidrar till större underskott. Förr eller senare kommer marknaden tvinga fram åtgärder som leder till åtstramning och lägre tillväxt. Högre räntor bidrar redan nu till åtstramning. Marknaden får än så länge sägas stå på optimisternas sida. CDS – som speglar marknadens bedömning av kreditrisk – ligger på måttliga och stabila nivåer, medan stabila eller till och med starka valutor för flera länder med höga räntor sänder samma signal. Sverige, som har EU:s lägsta 10-årsränta, har samtidigt fått en svagare valuta och något skifte mot säkra länder, som under eurokrisen, går inte att skönja. Varken centralbankerna eller marknaden verkar heller särskilt oroade för tillväxten.
I Tyskland fortsätter motgångarna för förbundskansler Friedrich Merz. 
I Mecklenburg-Vorpommern ser CDU ut att hamna under femprocentsspärren och därmed åka ur delstatsparlamentet, samtidigt som ytterhögerpartiet AfD blir största parti. CDU tappar också stort i Berlin, där vänsterpartiet Die Linke går starkast framåt och blir största parti. Trots den ökade pressen avvisar Merz än så länge krav på att avgå.
Förväntningarna på Norges Bank är splittrade
, men vi håller, med stor tvekan, fast vid att räntan höjs med 25 räntepunkter. Lite lägre inflation talar dock för att höjningen kan senareläggas. En majoritet i Bloombergs enkät räknar med en höjning, men nästan hälften tror på oförändrad ränta – och undertecknad lutar också åt en senare höjning. Mer om Norges Bank 
här.
Sverige
Riksbankens räntebesked och Penningpolitiska rapport i fokus
.
Alla analytiker tror på oförändrad ränta på torsdag och marknaden prisar bara in +4 punkter, men enligt vår ränteenkät finns det de som tror att räntan kan höjas nu i september. Vår prognos att Riksbanken ska vänta tills arbetsmarknaden vänder, innan räntan höjs, har fått stark motvind efter räntehöjningar från både Fed och ECB, som dessutom tolkades som hökaktiga av marknaden. Kanske ännu viktigare är de mycket kraftiga prisuppgångarna på drivmedel och elektricitet, som kommer att trycka upp inflationen betydligt under de närmaste månaderna. Riskerna mot vår prognos att räntebanan signalerar en tydlig men måttlig sannolikhet för en räntehöjning under de närmaste månaderna ligger på uppsidan. Till skillnad från de flesta andra centralbanker har Riksbanken framhållit att riskerna för inflation bör vägas mot risken att i onödan skada tillväxten. Hushållens konsumtion ser efter en lång period av stagnation ut att ta fart, men frågan är vad som händer om hushållen drabbas av både höga energipriser och högre räntor under de närmaste kvartalen. Riksbanken kan inte göra något åt en energidriven inflationsuppgång och, till skillnad från i många andra länder, kommer räntehöjningar dessutom att leda till högre KPI-inflation och högre hyror och bostadsrättsavgifter. Löneförhandlingarna, som inleds med krav från LO i oktober, kommer knappast heller att bli lättare av preventiva räntehöjningar. Di:s Skuggdirektion anser att räntan kan ligga still i september men skruvar upp planerna på räntehöjningar längre fram (mer 
här
 (betallänk).
Försöken att bilda regering har påbörjats 
och i fredags fick Magdalena Andersson, inte oväntat, det första av fyra försök att hitta en regering som en majoritet i riksdagen kan tolerera. Inledningen har inte varit särskilt optimistisk, där både Vänsterpartiet (V) och Centerpartiet (C) har hållit fast hårt vid de röda linjerna från valrörelsen. C har till och med sagt att V måste avstå från kravet på att sitta i regeringen för att man ens ska inleda samtal. Återstår att se hur mycket av utspelen som är förhandlingstaktik. Både C och V kan kanske i slutändan leva med en ren S-regering. Vilka politiska eftergifter som i så fall kommer att krävas, och hur C och V ska kunna enas om en budget, är betydligt svårare frågor. Magdalena Andersson ska redovisa resultatet av sina sonderingar den 28 september.

articles.title: Major defeat for Merz
articles.heading: Euro area outlook
articles.fulltext:
The far-right AfD made strong gains in the German state elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin. At the same time, Merz’s party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), appears to have suffered heavy losses. Confidence in Merz is low, but the Chancellor has dismissed speculation about his resignation.
Key points
Major defeat for CDU in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin
The far-right AfD makes strong gains
Chancellor Merz under heavy pressure, but for now he plans to stay in office
Pressure on Merz was already high ahead of today’s state elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin, following the CDU’s major setback in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt two weeks ago (read more 
here
).
Preliminary results show that the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) appears to have lost substantial support in 
Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania
, with the party only just clearing the 5% electoral threshold (13.3 per cent in 2021). The far-right AfD looks set to become the largest party, with 38% of the vote, more than double its share in 2021. The SPD, led by the popular Manuela Schwesig, the current Minister-President, is close behind with 36% of the vote.
In 
Berlin
, both the CDU and the Social Democrats have suffered significant losses, receiving around 20% and 12% of the vote respectively, compared with 28.2% and 18.4% in 2023. The big winners are The Left – after housing and rents became a key election issue – and the AfD, with 25.5% and 14.3% of the vote respectively. Overall, the AfD has made strong gains, continuing a trend seen in other state elections this year. In Saxony-Anhalt, the AfD may even be able to form a government.
Difficult coalition talks
In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, it appears possible to form a government without the AfD. One option would be for the popular Minister-President Schwesig to remain in office, with her party forming a coalition with the Greens and The Left.
In Berlin, the current governing coalition of the SPD and CDU no longer has sufficient support and would need to find an additional coalition partner, most likely the Greens or The Left, in order to keep the AfD out of government. Another possibility would be SPD governing with The Lefts and The Greens.
Merz remains in office
Ahead of today’s elections, speculation had increased over Merz’s future as Germany’s leader. Dissatisfaction with both the CDU and the current governing coalition is high. However, in comments following the election results, Merz has said that he intends to continue with his reform agenda.
Our main scenario is that Merz remains in office, although growing pressure from within his own party cannot be ruled out. In that case, Merz could choose to resign himself, or some form of confidence vote could take place. However, we are not there yet.

articles.title: Leaning towards a hike
articles.heading: Norges Bank Preview
articles.fulltext:
Uncertainty is unusually high ahead of Norges Bank’s Sep 24 rate decision, with expectations split. We lean towards a 25bps hike to 4.50% but see the decision as a very close call. Positive inflation developments over the summer have questioned the need for further tightening, while growth and labour market prospects remain stable and capacity utilization is drifting lower. However, inflation remains elevated, higher energy prices add to external price pressures, and higher rates abroad increase the risk of NOK weakness. We expect the Committee to retain a tightening bias, while making only minor changes to the rate path.
A really close call
Following Norges Bank’s policy shift in March, Norges Bank resumed rate hikes in May and lifted the rate path further in June to indicate a policy rate peak of 4.55% at the end of the year. Both the rate path and the Committee’s guidance pointed to a next rate hike by September. Positive inflation surprises during the summer have questioned the need for further policy tightening, and the Committee softened its guidance somewhat at the interim decision in August stating that “slower inflation is welcome news, but inflation is still too high, and it is too early to conclude that the inflation outlook has changed materially. It may thus still become necessary to raise the policy rate”. We regarded the reasoning on inflation as a tad hawkish, as it was emphasized that inflation is still markedly above target, and the rapid rise in business costs in recent years will contribute to keeping inflation elevated ahead. Moreover, the Committee noted that the average of the different underlying inflation indicators had fallen less and was somewhat higher than CPI-ATE inflation. The key question ahead of the upcoming Sep 24 rate decision is whether Norges Bank believes that the inflation outlook has changed materially. 
Developments in underlying inflation indicators have been a bit mixed; CPI-ATE increased to 3.0% y/y in August, narrowing the gap to Norges Bank’s trajectory to 0.3ppt below its estimate. Oil and gas prices are notably higher than assumed in June, but this is also reflected in a stronger-than-expected exchange rate. Meanwhile, growth and labour market prospects are stable while indicators from the regional network supports Norges Bank’s current assessment that capacity utilization is drifting lower. Overall, we believe data can pull the Committee in either direction and that the upcoming Sep 24th rate decision will be a really close call. On the one hand, a wait-and-see stance with clear indications of readiness to act on back of any deterioration in inflation prospects would maintain a steepness in the very front end of the curve while reducing the risk of restricting the economy more than needed. On the other, higher energy prices imply stronger external price pressures while also having lifted short rate expectations among trading partners – making the NOK vulnerable to a cautious policy stance. We acknowledge unusually high uncertainty but are leaning towards a 25bps hike to 4.50%. Expectations are divided though the median consensus estimate is for a 25bps hike (11 vs. 8). The market is viewing the decision as a 50/50 call judging by current pricing.
Below we conclude in detail regarding inflation and economic developments.
Positive inflation surprises enough?
Inflation has proven sticky and has remained above target for several years. The large downside surprise in CPI-ATE in 
June
, from 3.4% to 2.7% y/y, was thus positive. Inflation remained unexpectedly low in 
July
, running 0.6ppt below Norges Bank’s trajectory. The lower inflation during summer is mainly explained by food and other goods, with the latter probably being a correction after unusually large price increases during spring. The uptick in CPI-ATE to 3.0% y/y in 
August
 is explained by base effects from lower childcare fees in August last year, narrowing the gap to Norges Bank’s trajectory to 0.3ppt. The near-term forecast is thus likely to be lowered in the upcoming MPR. 
Changes to the long-term trajectory is more uncertain. Higher energy prices imply stronger external price impulses while also lending upside risk to wage growth in the medium term. However, this has also been reflected in the exchange rate though most recently the krone has weakened as NOK rates have lagged the repricing of policy rate expectations abroad. The import-weighted NOK index (i44) is on average so far in Q3 in line with Norges Bank’s estimate, but the spot level is 1.4% stronger than assumed. Both the bank’s assessment of the inflation pass-through from NOK (as discussed by Committee members in August) and the assumed i44 level (dependent on its expectations of market reaction to the decision) will be important for the medium-term inflation outlook.
Inflation expectations moderated somewhat in Q3. Business leaders’ CPI expectations, which Norges Bank views as a good indicator for domestic inflation, were on the contrary revised higher. CPI is seen at 4.2% in the next 12 months and 4.6% in 2 years. The latter was lifted by 0.5ppt and is high in a historical context. At the same time, wage growth expectations were revised down and is lower than Norges Bank’s estimates for 2026 and 2027. Wage growth expectations in the more important regional network were stable at 4.5% for this year while being lowered marginally to 4.0% in 2027, both aligning with Norges Bank’s forecast. We do not expect any major revisions to Norges Bank’s wage growth estimates, also reflecting that labour market developments have been broadly as envisaged.
Capacity utilization indicators have softened further. The contacts in the bank’s regional network reported a further decline in capacity constraints and labour shortages. Both are on aggregate below normal and aligns with Norges Bank’s assessment that the output gap will turn negative. This should, eventually, dampen domestic inflation pressures. Overall, we expect moderate revisions to the medium-term CPI-ATE forecast with inflation slowing only gradually and approaching towards the end of the forecasting period.
Somewhat weaker activity data
Activity data have been mixed but overall developments have not deviated markedly from Norges Bank’s projections. Below we summarize the most important developments since the Jun26 MPR.
Mainland GDP:
 Sequential growth in 
mainland GDP
 surprised on the downside in Q2, rising 0.3% q/q compared to Norges Bank’s 0.4% estimate. Growth was also revised lower for Q1, implying that mainland GDP is slightly lower than assumed by Norges Bank. However, excluding volatile non-cyclical sectors the underlying trend is not deviating materially from Norges Bank’s projections. Sentiment indicators have improved somewhat; 
consumer confidence
rebounded albeit from very depressed levels, and the Business Tendency Survey showed a slight improvement in manufacturing sentiment. Overall, however, the 
Regional Network Report
suggests stable growth momentum ahead with mainland GDP growth of 0.3% q/q in H2 which is in line with the bank
’s projection
. Recent 
household data
 points sideways. The trend in retail sales ex. autos appears to be little changed since the June26 MPR while on balance a little to the softer side as the 3m/3m rate now is slightly negative. Overall, household demand is broadly as envisaged.
Oil investment:
 Statistics Norway’s 
Oil Investment Survey
 for Q3 confirmed the narrative of a maturing cycle though operators revised their nominal investment estimate up in both 2026 and in 2027, implying that the downturn will be delayed until next year. Although the project pipeline is thinning, the survey included PDOs for three new development projects which will have the highest activity next year. We see upside risk to Norges Bank’s forecast for oil investments as it previously forecast a decline of 3% in 2026 and further by 5% in 2027. 
Wage growth:
 The 
Inflation Expectation Survey
 for Q3 points to easing wage pressures ahead, albeit from relatively high levels. Wage expectations were lowered and are set to align with the agreed-upon wage norm of 4.4% this year though a tad below Norges Bank’s 4.5% estimate for 2026. For next year, average wage growth is seen at 3.8%, 0.2pp below Norges Bank’s own estimate. Comparable estimates from the regional network are 4.5% and 4.0% respectively.
Labour market: 
Employment growth remains steady, rising 0.2% q/q in Q2, 0.1ppt above Norges Bank’s projections. Registered unemployment has been stable and in line with the bank’s projection. The increase in new registered vacancies seen in the beginning of the year has corrected, and the trend continues to point sideways. Survey indicators point to softer employment expectations and reduced recruitment difficulties. The LFS jobless rate was stable at 4.5% in July, but revision to previous months now point to unemployment having passed its peak. Overall, the labour market appears balanced, and Norges Bank is likely to continue forecast a slight increase in registered unemployment next year to above its estimate of NAIRU. 
Existing home prices:
 Existing home prices have been unusually volatile over the summer. Prices fell by a surprisingly large 1.1% m/m (SA) in 
July
, before rebounding by 0.8% m/m (SA) in 
August
. Norges Bank’s projected a 0.4% (SA) monthly increase in both July and August. While the August outcome partly reversed the July’s decline, the two releases combined remain softer than implied by the bank’s forecast and support a downward revision to its 3.5% y/y projection for existing home price growth in 2026. Norges Bank projects hefty price growth in the medium-term (6.5% in 2028 and 2029) as interest rates are approaching normal, but so far financial stability considerations are not a decisive factor. 
Global factors: 
Global uncertainty
 remains elevated. The US and Iran war have been through various peace agreements over the summer, though targeted strikes have intensified in recent weeks and prospects for a comprehensive settlement remain limited, at least until the US midterm election. Implications for both commodity prices and the NOK remain uncertain. We thus expect the bank to refrain from drawing too firm conclusions at this stage, and the Committee will continue 
monitoring various commodity prices and their spillovers to other goods and services prices ahead.
Futures prices for both brent oil and natural gas are significantly higher since Jun26 MPR. Rising inflation risks have spilled over to higher global policy rate expectations and longer yields. 
Tightening bias maintained
Norges Bank is once again likely to stress that uncertainty to the outlook is substantial, especially concerning the global outlook and energy prices. We also see high uncertainty related to possible changes to the rate path. Activity data has been somewhat weaker though underlying momentum appears broadly as envisaged, and the labour market remains healthy. We expect only minor revisions to Norges Bank’s assessment of the output gap. Meanwhile, the short-term inflation trajectory will in isolation lower the front end of the rate path, but inflation will remain high further out underpinned by still high wage growth. Moreover, energy prices and the NOK pull in different directions. Finally, higher rates abroad will lift the long end of the rate path. Overall, we expect minor changes to the rate path; marginally lower or unchanged in the front end, while slightly higher in the long end. Given that the current rate path peaks at 4.55%, a more pronounced lowering in the front end would in such case have justified an unchanged policy rate at the upcoming decision.
Current market pricing is underscoring the uncertainty ahead of the upcoming decision, implying near a 50/50 call. High energy prices have triggered a hawkish response from the ECB and the Fed, resulting in a repricing of rate hike expectations abroad. This has also lifted NOK rates, although to a much lesser extent. The market now discounts a policy rate peak around 4.60% while rate cuts have been postponed and the terminal rate lifted. Given the uncertainty ahead of the decision, large market moves are likely while the extent will be dependent on the outcome, guidance and rate path. We believe a rate hike, i.e., confirming inflation concerns, would open for the market to discount a higher policy rate peak. Meanwhile, the NOK is trading on primarily natural gas prices and looks increasingly stretched from a rate spread and positioning perspective. Arguably the NOK should nonetheless be more responsive to a dovish surprise. For more on our market views, see our latest 
Norway 360 report
. Regardless of the outcome of the upcoming decision, we believe Norges Bank is approaching the rate peak in this cycle. Eventually, as energy prices correct lower and inflation gradually eases, rate cuts should commence. We expect the policy rate to peak at 4.50%, followed by a gradual normalization from late 2027 and forecast a policy rate of 3.75% by end-2028.

articles.title: Policy rates decisions and Trump-Xi summit in focus
articles.heading: The Week Ahead
articles.fulltext:
Interest rate decisions by the Riksbank and Norges Bank will be the main focus next week. We expect Norges Bank to raise its policy rate by 25bp and believe that the Riksbank is moving closer to a rate hike, although we think it will take somewhat longer. On the political front, the key event will be the summit between US President Trump and Chinese President Xi. German state elections will also be important to follow.  
US:
No major data releases. September PMIs will be watched for signs of continued strong economic momentum. Several Fed officials are also due to speak, providing further clues regarding the Fed’s next policy move, following the hawkish signals in the September projections. Notably, NY Fed’s John Williams is scheduled to make three appearances. He was among the more dovish FOMC members ahead of the September decision.
Euro area:
Flash PMIs will be the main event. German Ifo, France Insee and consumer confidence will also provide insights to gauge business and consumer mood. Finally, 
we will keep a close eye on the German state elections in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania and Berlin (both on 20 September).
Sweden:
The quarterly inflation expectations report will be the last important information ahead of the highlight of the week – the Riksbank’s rate decision and policy report on Thursday. August producer prices (PPI) are published on Friday. 
Norway:
Norges Bank’s upcoming 24 September rate decision will be a really close call. While softer inflation developments and easing capacity pressures argue for keeping the policy rate unchanged, inflation remains well above target, energy prices and foreign policy rates have risen, and the Committee has retained a clear tightening bias. We acknowledge unusually high uncertainty but are leaning towards a 25bp rate hike to 4.50 per cent.

articles.title: BOJ Hikes But Dissent Caps Pace
articles.heading: Central Bank Insights
articles.fulltext:
Bank of Japan delivered an expected 25 bps rate hike to 1.25%. The 7-2 vote split underscores political discomfort with faster tightening. This dissent caps the hiking cycle at a quarterly pace at best, positioning December as the next live meeting with 60% probability. To sustain recent market pricing, Governor Ueda must deliver a sufficiently hawkish message. Any dovish shift risks forcing a repricing of December expectations and sending USD/JPY back towards 160.
Bank of Japan (BOJ) delivered an expected 25bps hike to 1.25%, with a 7-2 vote split. 
With the market pricing in more than 98% probability before the announcement, the hike itself was not in doubt. The risk was in the policy statement and the number of dissenters. The dissenting votes came from Asada Toichiro and Sato Ayano, who are both Takaichi cabinet appointees. 
The dissenting votes reflect the discomfort of the government regarding the faster pace of tightening. 
Chart 1: BOJ hiked as expected even with August inflation easing below 2%
Source: CEIC, SEB
The presence of 2 dissenters suggests a quarterly hike, at best. 
Given that markets assumed that today’s hike was essentially a done deal, the risks were already tilted to yen weakness
. 
With market already pricing in around 1 hike per quarter, there was little room for a hawkish surprise. If the dissenters get their way, they may prompt the market to slowly fade the quarterly hike expectations. Further complicating the outlook is the expiration of terms of two known hawks over the next 10 months, Takata Hajime and Tamura Naoki. New appointees will likely turn the bias of the BOJ board to a less hawkish stance. 
For now, December is the next live meeting with a significant probability at around 60%.
Chart 2: BOJ expectations have risen materially in the last 6 months
Source: Bloomberg, SEB
Expectations on BOJ policy rate have materially risen over the past 6 months
. After the policy meeting in March 2026, markets were pricing in 1.8 hikes through December 2026, with the policy rate expected to reach 1.19% by end-2026. Latest expectations point to less than 3 more hikes over the next 12 months taking the policy rate to 1.43% by yearend, with further upside to 1.87% by July 2027. The curve has shifted by 40 to 74 bps across all tenors (Chart 2). Even so, the 2s10s part of the curve had steepened by almost 16bps even as the 10s30s segment flattened by around 14bps. 
While the front-end of the curve rose on changes to rate hike expectations, the long-end remained anchored to the fiscal risks and lower BOJ bond purchases.
Chart 3: Recent widening of US-Japan bond spreads does not bode well for the yen
Source: Bloomberg, SEB
Governor Ueda will need to sound sufficiently hawkish to convince the market that every quarter is live for a hike. 
Although BOJ hawk Takata Hajime recently raised the possibility of back-to back moves, it is unlikely that the pace of tightening will be further accelerated given the dissenters. Indeed, the room to raise expectations on the terminal rate has narrowed. In comparison, expectations on the Federal Reserve have much more room to rise. Recent widening of the US-Japan yield spreads (Chart 3) reflect how BOJ tightening expectations have been crowded out by the narrative from the Federal Reserve. 
Any hint from Governor Ueda of softening of language regarding the pace of future hikes could trigger a repricing of the December meeting and push USD/JPY back towards 160.

articles.title: Stocks rise, new Fed forecast and "triple witching"
articles.heading: Nordic Alert
articles.fulltext:
Global key stories
The US stock markets rose yesterday (S&P 500 +1.1%; Nasdaq +1.7%) as market interest rates fell, and lower oil prices – possibly linked to some 
news
 of renewed diplomatic attempts – strengthened optimism that inflation could be kept under control the day after the Federal Reserve hiked interest rates. The euro strengthened slightly against the dollar and the price of gold rose.
The Trump administration yesterday approved the sale of F-35 fighter jets to Saudi Arabia worth US$24.3 billion. However, Congress still needs to approve the deal. Some concerns have been expressed about whether Saudi Arabia's security relations with China could lead to the transfer of the underlying technology. 
We change our forecast and assess that the Fed will make another hike in December.
 The Fed's rate hike on Wednesday was accompanied by hawkish signals in both the Fed members' own forecasts and in the comments of Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who echoed many of his arguments from Jackson Hole. The fact that almost all members of the Fed are forecasting at least one more hike this year suggests that the committee thinks a hike is not enough and that new increases in energy prices are worrying members. As before, we believe that underlying inflationary pressures will continue to subside next year. This, in our opinion, paves the way for another cut at the end of 2027, followed by two cut steps in March and June 2028, to a level of 3.25-3.50%. Read more 
here
. 
New forecast also for the Bank of England.
 Yesterday, the central bank left its policy rate unchanged at 3.75% while signalling greater concern about the spillover effects from higher energy prices. We are therefore changing our forecast and now expect a hike in November, but are adamant that interest rate cuts will begin in Q4 2027. Read more 
here
. 
As expected, the Bank of Japan today raised interest rates
 by 25 basis points to 1.25%. The bank's comments in connection with the decision did not give clear indications that the Board was considering a further rate hike at its next meeting in October. The market had expected a more hawkish communication and the Japanese yen has therefore weakened after the announcement. 
Markets today are also facing so-called "triple witching"
 – when derivative contracts linked to stocks, index options and futures expire quarterly. Options with a nominal value of over $2 trillion expire today, and this can create unusually high trading volume and sometimes heightened volatility towards closing, especially in the last hour of trading when fund managers and institutions adjust or roll their positions at the same time.
More news related to the Ukraine war.
 Parliamentary elections begin today in non-democratic Russia and will continue until September 20. In Copenhagen
, the 
NATO Military Committee Conference
 will start, 
 where the members' commanders are expected to discuss a further strengthening of the alliance's collective deterrence and defense, innovation and technology, as well as support for Ukraine. The EU decided yesterday to send EUR 3.3 billion to Ukraine to procure missiles and drones. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned on the same day that Russia plans to carry out "hybrid" drone and missile attacks against countries that support Ukraine, including NATO member Poland. Tusk said there is a real risk that drones or other types of missiles could fly into the territory of one or more NATO countries on the eastern flank and even cause destruction. Several of the country's airports have experienced disruptions in recent days.
On the agenda 
in addition to the above,
economic statistics mainly include German producer price inflation and US industrial production. In addition, informal meetings of EU finance ministers and central bank governors are being held today, and updated credit ratings are expected today for Greece (Moody's), Poland (Moody's) and Sweden (Fitch). 
Worth reading from SEB
: 
FI & FX Strategy
 and comments on Norges Bank's 
network report
. 
Nordic key stories
Our investor survey ahead of the Riksbank's interest rate meeting shows that the majority do not expect a hike next week.
On the other hand, almost everyone expects higher interest rates in December, and in the longer term, expectations differ. 
The government formation process is underway.
 Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson yesterday requested his resignation, which started the actual government formation process. Speaker Andreas Norlén accepted the request and announced that he will today hold private talks with representatives of the parliamentary parties. Magdalena Andersson (Social Democratic Party) has invited the other three opposition parties to a group discussion.

articles.title: Starkare börs, ny Fed-prognos och ”triple witching”
articles.heading: Morning Alert
articles.fulltext:
Internationellt
De amerikanska börserna steg igår (S&P 500 +1,1%; Nasdaq +1,7%) samtidigt som marknadsräntor föll, och ett lägre oljepris – eventuellt kopplat till vissa 
nyheter
 om förnyade diplomatiska försök – stärkte optimismen om att inflationen kan hållas under kontroll dagen efter att Federal Reserve höjde räntorna. Euron stärktes svagt mot dollarn och priset på guld steg.
Trumpadministrationen godkände igår försäljning av stridsflyg av klassen F-35 till Saudiarabien till ett värde av USD 24,3 miljarder. Kongressen behöver dock fortfarande godkänna avtalet. Viss oro har uttryckts över huruvida Saudiarabiens säkerhetsförbindelser med Kina kan leda till överföring av den underliggande teknologin. 
Vi ändrar prognos och bedömer att Fed gör ytterligare en höjning i december.
 Feds räntehöjning i onsdags åtföljdes av hökaktiga signaler i både Fed-ledamöternas egna prognoser och i kommentarerna från Feds ordförande Kevin Warsh, som upprepade många av sina argument från Jackson Hole. Att nästan alla ledamöter i Fed prognostiserar minst en höjning till i år tyder på att kommittén tycker att en höjning inte räcker samt att nya uppgångar i energipriserna oroar ledamöterna. Vi tror liksom tidigare att underliggande inflationstryck kommer att fortsätta att dämpas nästa år. Det banar, enligt oss, väg för en ny sänkning i slutet av 2027, följt av två sänkningssteg under mars och juni 2028, till en nivå på 3,25-3,50%. Läs mer 
här
. 
Ny prognos även för Bank of England.
 Centralbanken lämnade igår styrräntan oförändrad på 3,75% samtidigt som man signalerade större oro över spridningseffekterna från de högre energipriserna. Vi ändrar därmed vår prognos och räknar nu med en höjning i november, men står fast vid att räntesänkningar inleds under Q4 2027. Läs mer 
här
. 
Den japanska centralbanken höjde idag som väntat räntan
 med 25 punkter till 1,25%. Bankens kommentarer i samband med beslutet gav inga tydliga indikationer på att direktionen övervägde en ytterligare räntehöjning vid sitt nästa möte i oktober. Marknaden hade förväntat sig en mer hökaktig kommunikation och den japanska yenen har därför försvagats efter beskedet. 
Marknaderna står idag också inför så kallad ”triple witching”
 – då derivatkontrakt kopplade till aktier, indexoptioner och terminer förfaller kvartalsvis. Optioner med ett nominellt värde på över 2 biljoner dollar förfaller idag, och det kan skapa ovanligt hög handelsvolym och ibland förhöjd volatilitet mot stängning, särskilt under den sista handelstimmen när fondförvaltare och institutioner justerar eller rullar sina positioner samtidigt.
Flera nyheter relaterade till Ukrainakriget.
 Parlamentsval påbörjas idag i icke-demokratin Ryssland och håller på till den 20:e september. I Köpenhamn startar 
NATO Military Committee Conference
 där medlemmarnas överbefälhavare väntas diskutera en ytterligare förstärkning av alliansens kollektiva avskräckning och försvar, innovation och teknik samt stöd till Ukraina. EU beslutade igår att skicka EUR 3,3 miljarder till Ukraina för att upphandla missiler och drönare. Polens premiärminister Donald Tusk varnade samma dag för att Ryssland planerar att genomföra drönar- och missilattacker av ”hybridtyp” mot länder som stöder Ukraina, däribland Nato-medlemmen Polen. Tusk sade att det finns en reell risk att drönare eller andra typer av missiler kan flyga in på ett eller flera Nato-länders territorium på den östra flanken och till och med orsaka förstörelse. Flera av landets flygplatser har upplevt störningar de senaste dagarna.
På dagordningen 
förutom ovanstående
märks bland ekonomiska statistik främst tysk producentprisinflation och amerikansk industriproduktion. Därutöver hålls idag informella möten mellan EU:s finansministrar och centralbankschefer och uppdaterade kreditvärderingsbetyg väntas idag för Grekland (Moody’s), Polen (Moody’s) och Sverige (Fitch). 
Läsvärt från SEB
: 
FI & FX Strategy
 samt kommentar till Norges Banks 
nätverksrapport
. 
Sverige
Vår investerarundersökning inför Riksbankens räntemöte visar att majoriteten inte förväntar höjning nästa vecka.
Däremot räknar nästan alla med högre räntor i december och på längre sikt går förväntningarna isär. Läs mer 
här
. 
Regeringsbildningsprocessen är igång.
 Statsminister Ulf Kristersson begärde igår sitt entledigande, vilket satte igång själva regeringsbildningsprocessen. Talman Andreas Norlén tog emot begäran och meddelade att han idag kommer att samtala enskilt med företrädare för riksdagspartierna. Magdalena Andersson (S) har bjudit in de andra tre oppositionspartierna till ett gruppsamtal.

articles.title: Most expect no change in September
articles.heading: SEB Investor Survey
articles.fulltext:
*** See attachment for full report ***
Most expect no change in September, but almost all see higher rates by December
A wide majority of
 respondents expect the Riksbank to keep the policy rate at 1.75% in 
September
. 
A minority of 12% predict a rate hike to 2.00%.
Further out, expectations diverge. While 42% expect the policy rate to remain unchanged at 1.75% in November, 54% the policy rate to be 2.00% by then and 4% see the policy rate at 2.25%.
Almost all expect (at least) one rate hike by December
Most (80%) expect one hike to 2.00%, but a few predict two, or even three hikes by December. A thin minority expect the rate to remain at 1.75% in December. The expectations for the policy rate in December have shifted markedly higher since August.
Further out, expectations continue to diverge substantially. In December 2027, expectations span 1.50-2.75%. Apart from a very small minority, which expect the Riksbank will have cut to 1.5%, almost all respondents expect the policy rate to be above the current level. The median expectation in December 2027 remains at 2.25%, which is the same as in August.
Most expect the Riksbank to raise the rate path significantly
The Riksbank will publish a new rate path at the September meeting. The June rate path reaches 1.87% by December, signalling 50% probability of a rate hike this year.
Respondents generally expect a steeper rate path than the Riksbank’s June path. The median expectation is for the Riksbank to lift the implied rate from 1.87% to 2.00% in December 2026, and from 2.02% to 2.23% in December 2027. In November, the median expectation is 1.90%.
There are also expectations of both a slightly lower and a substantially higher rate path. The high scenario expects a rate hike in September, a considerable likelihood of another in November and some probability of a third by the end of the year, reaching 2.30 by December. The policy rate thereafter rises gradually to 2.50% in 2027. The lowest estimate expects very gradually rising policy rate over the coming year, 
similar to
 the Riksbank’s June path.
SEB anticipate a steeper policy rate path compared to June, signalling 60% probability (15bps) of a hike over the coming three policy meetings. Further out, the new path is anticipated to reflect a higher probability of a total of two hikes in 2027-2028 compared to June, levelling out around the mid-point of the Riksbank’s estimated interval for the neutral policy rate. 
Read more in our 
Riksbank Preview

articles.title: A perfect storm
articles.heading: SEB FI & FX Strategy
articles.fulltext:
At a glance:
In market focus.
 Geopolitics; Trump-Xi summit (24 September); euro-area CPI releases (week beginning 28 September).
Global macro and risk appetite. 
Geopolitics returned to centre stage as US-Iran hostilities have escalated and the Houthis have taken control of a strategically important stretch of Red Sea coastline. Brent has moved above USD 100/bbl. Risk assets have reacted negatively, while bond yields have risen sharply, driven by more hawkish policy rate expectations and fiscal concerns. For markets, the key issue is now the energy price outlook. President Trump has limited scope to escalate but equally lacks a politically viable route to a formal exit on acceptable terms. Our base case remains a prolonged status quo, with Brent retreating towards the USD 80-100/bbl range. The adverse scenario would be a disruption to Saudi oil flows through the Red Sea, potentially pushing Brent above its spring highs. Conversely, a more constructive outcome would involve a US military withdrawal from the region, leaving regional actors to establish a framework for reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
US macro: Continued resilience.
 Strong August payrolls and retail sales support the prevalent view within the Fed that current rates were not restrictive. We continue to see risks of a slowdown in consumer spending given that the support from tax refunds is fading, household purchasing power is hit by higher gasoline prices and the savings rate is already low. However, equity prices/wealth effects remain supportive. Some labour market indicators have also strengthened recently. We share the view that the Fed will deliver one more hike this year. The burden of proof has shifted from what would force the Fed to hike, to what would stop the Fed from tightening a bit more. We continue to believe that underlying inflation trends will improve next year as temporary shocks from tariffs and energy prices and, to some extent, on IT from the AI buildout, pass. The recent escalation of the conflict in the Middle East and renewed upward pressure on energy prices is an uncertain factor, however.
USD short rates: Peak hawkishness reached? 
The Fed unanimously raised its policy rate target range to 3.75-4.00% this week. The dot plot signals one further hike this year and leaves open the possibility of another in 2027. With markets discounting 75bp of additional tightening by summer 2027, we think the balance of risks for rates has shifted to the downside relative to current forward pricing.
USD bonds: Time for consolidation.
 The re-escalation of the Middle East conflict has pushed bond yields higher, while this week’s hawkish Fed message added to the pressure. With short positioning stretched and Fed pricing aggressive, we expect the 10Y Treasury yield to consolidate in a 4.90-5.10% range for now.
Euro area macro: Will sentiment indicators continue to signal resilient growth? 
Survey data suggest that growth momentum has strengthened despite the war in the Middle East, summer wildfires and droughts. The improvement has been driven mainly by manufacturing, while services PMI remains in expansionary territory. Higher energy prices pose risks to both inflation and activity as winter approaches.
EUR short-end: Hawkish enough. 
Forwards currently discount around 85bp of additional ECB hikes. We think it will be difficult for markets to push pricing materially further in a hawkish direction. At the same time, the market is likely to remain reluctant to price fewer than 75bp of additional hikes absent a decisive breakthrough that delivers a substantial and sustained fall in energy prices.
EUR bonds: A perfect bond-market storm. 
The bond sell-off has been driven by a repricing of the policy-rate outlook and broader structural forces, all pointing in the same direction. Given already hawkish ECB pricing, we think the US Treasury market will be the decisive driver for Bunds this autumn. Our base case is for the 10Y Bund yield to trade predominantly in the 3.40-3.60% range over the coming months.
EURUSD: Rates largely priced, energy decides the downside. 
EURUSD has broken lower, tracking a wider US-EUR 2Y spread as the Fed resumes hiking. 
With around 75bp of Fed hikes and 85bp of ECB hikes priced by mid-2027
, rates look largely priced, and we see more scope for the US leg to retrace as US data soften. Crowded short-duration positioning suggests that retracement could be fast. A sustained break below the June lows (1.133–1.136) would likely need an energy shock, such as a disruption to Saudi Red Sea flows or a cold winter, given the Euro's sensitivity to gas prices. Under-hedged dollar exposure keeps the medium-term skew USD-negative. With volatility low and wings cheap, our bias would be towards longer-dated low-delta EURUSD upside, while winter protection looks reasonably priced.
EUR rates: A perfect bond market storm
Following the bond market sell-off, which regained momentum over the past two weeks, we revisit the underlying drivers and our outlook for EUR rates as bond yields have moved materially above the extended-scenario targets we established in early March, shortly after the Iran conflict began (see 
SEB FI & FX: Market implications of a prolonged Iran conflict
, 6 March).
What did we say in early March? 
During the first week of the Iran conflict, we outlined targets for EUR and USD rates under an extended-conflict scenario lasting several months. The scenario assumed Brent crude trading around USD 100/bbl.
For such a scenario, we set the following targets:
German 10Y yield at 3.00-3.20%;
German 2Y yield at 2.70-2.80%;
ECB forwards discounting 50-75bp of rate hikes during 2026.
The chart below shows our corresponding early-March projections for 2Y and 10Y EUR swap rates.
SEB extended conflict scenario from 3 March: Brent USD 100/bbl (arrows show projection)
As the conflict dragged on, German 2Y and 10Y yields – as well as corresponding swap rates – tracked our initial scenario relatively closely through the summer. Developments since late August, however, have pushed rates materially above those projections.
Why have rates overshot? 
The initial repricing of the ECB policy outlook was completed in March. Thereafter, rate expectations fluctuated significantly through the summer, reflecting alternating optimism and disappointment regarding the prospects for a resolution to the conflict and the consequent outlook for energy prices.
A second major repricing wave followed Fed Governor Warsh’s Jackson Hole speech in late August. The subsequent re-escalation of the Iran conflict, together with the sharply hawkish market interpretation of the ECB’s 10 September meeting, added further upside to the expected policy rate path.    
ECB policy rate expectations discounted by forwards
This repricing has been reflected in both government bond yields and swap rates across the curve, as illustrated in the following chart for the German 10Y yield.
ECB policy rate expectations for the coming two years & German 10Y yield
Euro area yields have also faced substantial spillover pressure from the global bond sell-off, most notably the rise in US Treasury yields. While the repricing of Fed expectations has been a key driver, several additional factors have contributed: renewed concerns over long-term US fiscal sustainability; questions around the Fed’s commitment to its inflation target; uncertainty regarding international demand for Treasuries; and the implications of recent JPY intervention (see 
JPY intervention in focus
, 21 August).
As illustrated below, the Treasury sell-off has fed into long-dated German yields, compounding the underlying upward pressure from the repricing of the ECB outlook.
10Y yields: US & Germany
What next? 
The recent sell-off has been driven by a combination of central-bank expectations and broader structural forces, all pointing in the same direction and thereby reinforcing the rise in yields. Large fiscal deficits and increasing competition for capital – including from AI-related investment – are unlikely to disappear in the foreseeable future.
That said, with around 85bp (down from around 95bp immediately after the 10 September meeting of additional ECB tightening), discounted by summer 2027, we think current market pricing is sufficiently hawkish. As the hiking cycle progresses and the deposit rate approaches its terminal level, markets should eventually shift their focus from the extent of further hikes towards the timing and pace of subsequent cuts. At that point, policy-rate expectations could begin to offset the structural upward pressure on long-end yields stemming from elevated supply.
As we have discussed on several occasions, historical precedents suggest that long yields in both the US and the euro area tend to peak broadly around the time policy rates peak. The SEB house view currently incorporates two further ECB hikes, in December and March, whereas forwards discount policy tightening continuing until late summer 2027.
If the deposit rate peaks in March, long yields could also peak by early spring – particularly if the rise in long-dated Treasury yields loses momentum as we expect. If, instead, the ECB continues to hike through July 2027, the peak in long yields could be delayed towards mid-2027.
For the autumn, much will depend on developments in the Iran conflict and energy markets. Pricing close to four ECB hikes is aggressive enough that a modest softening in expectations is possible over the coming months. However, we expect the market to remain reluctant to price fewer than 75bp of additional hikes absent a decisive breakthrough that delivers a substantial and sustained fall in energy prices.
Assuming that markets fluctuate around a terminal deposit-facility rate of 3.25-3.50% this autumn, we expect the German 10Y yield to trade predominantly in a 3.40-3.60% range. In our view, the main upside risk to that range would come from a renewed Treasury sell-off rather than a further material hawkish repricing of ECB expectations.
ECB policy rates & German 10y yield
When will the ECB resume bond purchases?
 The ECB is currently reviewing the parameters of its operational framework. We expect the outcome to be published in late 2026 or, more likely, in early 2027. The review should provide further guidance on the desired mix between refinancing operations and securities purchases in supplying liquidity to the Eurosystem, as well as on the likely composition, size and maturity profile of the future securities portfolio.
ECB communication since the announcement of the new operational framework in early 2024 (see Say hello to the next-generation hybrid Eurosystem!, 13 March 2024) has been clear: it intends first to introduce structural refinancing operations as a complement to existing weekly and monthly refinancing operations. Securities purchases for a new structural portfolio would follow only thereafter.
We therefore think new ECB purchases are unlikely to begin before late 2027 at the earliest. They will consequently offer little relief from the prevailing structural pressure on bond markets any time soon.
EURUSD: Rates largely priced, energy decides the downside
EURUSD has broken lower, tracking a wider US-EUR 2Y spread as the Fed resumes hiking. With c.75bp of Fed hikes and c.85bp of ECB hikes priced by mid-2027, rates look largely priced, and we see more scope for the US leg to retrace as US data soften. Crowded short-duration positioning suggests that retracement could be fast. A sustained break below the June lows (1.133–1.136) would likely need an energy shock, such as a disruption to Saudi Red Sea flows or a cold winter, given the euro's high gas beta. Under-hedged dollar exposure keeps the medium-term skew USD-negative. With vol low and wings cheap, our bias would be towards longer-dated low-delta EURUSD upside, while winter protection looks reasonably priced.
Near term, we see scope for EURUSD to move back into the 1.15–1.18 range if Fed pricing eases. European risks, mainly winter energy and to a lesser extent French politics, could keep the pair near the lower end for longer. Our longer-term view, including scenarios and triggers for a break of the range, is outlined in our latest 
FX Pilot.
The dollar is trading the front end, not fiscal risk.
 The Fed hiked 25bp unanimously, and the dots signalled one more hike this year. Warsh's hawkish press conference sold off the front end and flattened the curve, and the dollar rose. This fits the pattern since late July: the dollar has tracked the US front end and the curve more closely than 10Y yields, consistent with a Fed-driven move rather than a fiscal one. A re-steepening as Fed pricing eases would be the dollar-negative mirror image.
EURUSD is following the 2Y spread, and the US leg is driving it.
 Both curves have repriced since late August, and each now discounts roughly 75-85bp of hikes by mid-2027. The rise in US 2Y rates has been larger, however, widening the differential, and EURUSD has followed it below its range. ECB pricing has offered only a partial offset, easing back from its post-meeting highs.
The Fed is hiking, but pricing is running ahead of the data. 
The Fed raised rates to 3.75–4.00% unanimously, and the dots signal one more hike this year. Market pricing held steady through the summer even as US data surprises eased from their spring/early summer highs, suggesting a Hormuz premium in the price. September then brought a further repricing, well beyond the modest rebound in payrolls and retail sales. The burden of proof has shifted to what would stop the Fed, but pricing has moved further than the data justify, and underlying inflation should slow in 2027 as tariff and energy shocks pass. I.e. rate support for the dollar looks close to peaking, and the Fed hiking less than discounted is the main medium-term USD risk.
Retracement risk is skewed towards the US leg. 
Our house view has one more Fed hike and two from the ECB (December, March), so both curves look stretched. But the unwind is unlikely to be symmetric. Markets are likely to resist pricing fewer than 75bp from the ECB without a clear fall in energy prices. Against our house view, that leaves c.50bp of potential Fed unwind, compared with only c.10bp before ECB pricing (c.85bp) reaches that level. If US consumption slows as we expect, a narrower spread would bring EURUSD back into its range.  
Rates positioning is crowded, and that raises the risk of a sharp retracement.
 Our CTA proxies show trend followers heavily short duration across the US and Europe (futures around -0.8, swaps paid around +0.8), and the position was extended further last week. That leaves little room for more selling and makes both curves vulnerable to a squeeze if energy prices or data turn. Positioning is similar in the two front ends, however, so it doesn't indicate which leg leads. Positioning mainly suggests any retracement could be fast.
Energy is the main risk to a return into the range.
 The euro has the highest gas beta in G10, and it heads into winter with TTF elevated and storage is below seasonal norms, though adaptation means c.70% is likely sufficient. Our base case has brent easing towards USD 80–100/bbl, and adaptation, Asian coal substitution and resilient euro area surveys provide partial offsets. A disruption to Saudi flows through the Red Sea would hit the euro twice: directly through terms of trade, and by keeping the Hormuz premium in Fed pricing.
French politics is a slow burn rather than a trigger.
 The OAT-Bund spread has widened to around 95bp, reflecting fiscal and political risk ahead of the draft 2027 budget at end-September and the presidential election next spring. So far the euro has looked through this, and the correlation between the spread and EURCHF has faded. A Le Pen win could be read as relatively market-friendly, so the real risk is a candidate (Mélenchon) arguing for debt cancellation with the ECB. With public support for the EU and the euro at multi-year highs, the election may prove a wall of worry the euro can climb. Budget slippage would keep a spread premium in place, but we see it as a drag on the euro rather than a trigger.
Positioning is turning short EURUSD. 
Our CTA proxy has moved into short EURUSD territory (-0.37), and last week trend followers added USD longs across G10. There is room for this to extend: repositioning to max short would be consistent with EURUSD around 1.10, in line with our downside scenario.
But 
the dollar remains structurally over-owned.
 The medium-term picture looks different. The broad dollar signal is still net short (DXY -0.18) despite last week's covering, and implicit USD exposure via unhedged assets has grown as FX hedge ratios have fallen. Once Fed pricing turns, this combination (spec shorts in EURUSD, under-hedged real-money dollar holdings) is fuel for a larger dollar move lower.
Options offer convexity to both a winter drop and a 2027 turn.
 Implied vol is rather low across tenors, with 1Y ATM around 6.3%. Realised vol is turning up from lows near 4%. Wings are not bid up, though both 1Y and 3M 10-delta butterflies have started to tick up from recent lows, suggesting demand for tail protection is building. Levels remain close to long-run averages. Risk reversals are near flat across tenors, and the term structure is steep, which makes short-dated optionality relatively cheap. Neither a winter energy shock nor a sharp rates retracement looks priced, crowded rates positioning and building FX shorts positioning means either could come fast. I.e. regardless of view, options look like an attractive way to express it. For the 2027 dollar view, our bias would be towards longer-dated, low-delta EURUSD upside. For those concerned about the winter path, low-delta downside protection into Q1 also looks reasonably priced.

articles.title: Energy prices force BoE to hike in November
articles.heading: Bank of England
articles.fulltext:
The BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75% in a 6–3 vote, unchanged from the July meeting. The overall message was more cautious, with the MPC expressing increased concern about second-round effects materialising and placing greater emphasis on headline inflation, particularly the impact of energy prices. Markets interpreted the hold as slightly dovish and scaled back around 4bp of tightening at the November meeting. We are revising our forecast to include an insurance hike in November but sticking with our call of cuts starting in Q4 2027. 
MPC more nervous about energy prices
The BoE held Bank Rate at 3.75%, with Mann, Pill and Greene voting for a hike, as at the previous meeting.
The previous guidance on inflation risks stemming from the Middle East conflict was reiterated, with Bailey stating that risks are tilted to the upside and that “if the conflict in the Middle East persists for an extended period, as appears to be the case, and the risk of second-round effects emerging increases, it is likely that policy may have to tighten”.
Currently, second-round effects do not appear material enough to warrant a policy response, although the probability has increased since the July meeting. Notably, the relatively confident stance on underlying inflation has been toned down, while greater emphasis is being placed on headline CPI, which remains elevated.
Higher market interest rates faced by households and businesses will act to reduce inflation over time, providing sufficient disinflationary pressure according to some MPC members, while others argue that this does not adequately substitute for an increase in Bank Rate.
Dovish market reaction reflects sentiment, not communication
: Markets scaled back around 4–7bp of tightening across the curve, with the November contract retracing 4bp and indicating an 82% probability of a hike at the next meeting. The dovish reaction should probably be seen as a reflection of the extremely hawkish pricing going into the meeting rather than the decision itself. GBP initially weakened by 0.3% against both the USD and EUR but has since recovered somewhat.
Energy prices and second round effects is the only thing that matters.
 The conflict in the Middle East and its impact on energy prices and the UK economy remain the dominant sources of uncertainty for the inflation outlook. The MPC argues that Bank Rate cannot reduce global energy prices, but policy needs to balance the cost of leaning too little against potential inflationary pressures with the cost to economic activity of leaning too much.
Current spot prices are more consistent with the adverse scenario presented in the July MPR, which would imply a Bank Rate closer to 4.25%. CPI inflation has risen from 2.6% to 3.1% over the past three months and is expected to reach close to 4.0%, also broadly in line with the adverse scenario. BoE research shows that non-linear effects, including pass-through to consumers, are more likely when inflation exceeds 4%, which is where inflation is now heading.
Labour market, financial conditions and activity: 
There is still slack in the labour market, while tight financial conditions are providing a meaningful degree of monetary restraint. However, stronger-than-expected activity increases the risk that firms will be able to pass higher energy costs on to consumers. Unemployment remains unchanged at 4.9%, and while the degree of slack is uncertain, the MPC now judges that it has at least stabilised as activity has strengthened.
Growth has accelerated recently, with activity stronger than the MPC had expected. This makes the demand environment more supportive of cost pass-through and therefore raises the risk that higher energy prices feed more broadly into inflation. For some MPC members, tighter financial conditions and their pass-through to retail rates provide sufficient restraint for now, while others argue that this is not a substitute for an increase in Bank Rate.
Our decision:
 Energy prices will determine whether the BoE hikes Bank Rate at the next policy meeting on 5 November, making the outlook highly binary, but still surrounded by significant uncertainty given its dependence on developments in the Middle East. In our base case, the Strait of Hormuz remains closed until at least the US midterms on 3 November. We therefore do not expect a swift decline in energy prices over the coming month, which should prompt the BoE to hike at the November meeting.
We view this as an 
insurance hike
, aimed at containing the risk of second-round effects from the energy shock. The MPC would clearly prefer to keep Bank Rate unchanged, but persistently high energy prices are likely to force its hand. If elevated energy prices and uncertainty persist, another hike before year-end cannot be ruled out.
At the same time, the underlying fundamentals remain soft, particularly in the labour market, while tight financial conditions should continue to weigh on employment and activity. We therefore maintain our view that the BoE will resume cutting rates next year, but have pushed the start of the easing cycle back to September, followed by cuts in December and February 2028.
QT update: 
The MPC decided to reduce the APF (Asset Purchase Facility) to zero,
 with the stock set to decline by around £46bn per year through gilt maturities and 
£20bn of outright sales
. Gilts maturing before 2035 will be held to maturity, while £120bn of the longest-dated gilts will remain on the APF to indirectly back banknote issuance.
Of the remaining £146bn, consisting of gilts maturing between 2035–49, the BoE plans to unwind 
£20bn per year
 and is reviewing a model where the 
DMO purchases these gilts directly from the APF at market prices
. APF auctions are paused until the review is completed by April 2027.
So 
the big news is
that the BoE is planning to sell long-dated Gilts directly to the DMO
 (i.e. the government), rather than the private market, thereby avoiding additional supply pressure where liquidity is thin and rates are relatively high. The DMO purchases would probably be financed through increased issuance at the short end and potentially the very long end, helping to ease pressure on the more stretched part of the curve, as illustrated by the 5y forward swap curve below.

articles.title: Softer, but no drama
articles.heading: Norwegian Regional Network Report
articles.fulltext:
Norges Bank’s Regional Network Report sends a somewhat softer message, pointing to stable output expectations and moderately lower capacity pressure and labour shortages. Moreover, wage growth expectations for 2027 were lowered marginally to align with Norges Bank’s estimate. Overall, the network signals that developments are (gradually) moving in the right direction. However, this aligns with Norges Bank’s current assessment, and we are thus not convinced that this will be enough for Norges Bank to argue for underlying inflation drivers having changed materially. To conclude, we stick with our call for a final rate hike to 4.50% at the upcoming rate decision though underscoring that it is a really close call.
Details: 
Output expectations:
 The regional network shows stable output growth expectation of 0.3% in Q3 and Q4, aligning with Norges Bank’s own projection for Q3. All sectors, except for oil services, expect higher activity ahead. Oil services remain pessimistic, though output expectations have been revised up by a modest 0.1pp to -0.1%. On the other side is the household services sector, which have revised their growth expectations up by 0.2pp, now expecting 0.7% growth in Q3 largely due to solid activity in tourism. The construction sector has lowered their growth expectations by 0.2pp, expecting Q3 growth to rise by a modest 0.1%. Overall, the aggregated output indicator continues to point to broadly stable growth momentum ahead.
Looking into the details, events in connection with the football World Cup have likely boosted output in the beginning of the summer. A number of respondents report high guest counts within hotels and restaurants while some are reporting that increased tourism has boosted retail trade growth. At the same time some retailers report that prospects for higher rates have likely contributed to lower turnover growth in consumer durables. Several car dealers expect new car sales to pick up towards the end of 2026, when new tax rules are expected to come into force, but sales will nevertheless be weaker than in 2025. Large increases in investments related to defense and emergency preparedness continue to boost commercial services. Meanwhile, construction activity remains low though having picked up in the South-West region. Many believe that construction has troughed, but at the same time the upturn keeps getting delayed. Finally, the fall in activity in the oil suppliers sector partly reflects few new major field developments. As reported in the Q3 oil investment survey, the fall is being dampened by maintenance, modifications and operating within existing fields on stream. Some also cite strong growth in drilling and subsea activity on both the Norwegian continental shelf and in some export markets. 
Investment expectations:
 Contacts revised their investment expectations significantly higher and on aggregate expect a 1.6% increase in 2026 (prev. 0.4%) and 2.6% increase in 2027 (prev.0.2%). Data centers buildout is pulling investments among service contacts up this year and will contribute to accelerating growth in 2027. Technology investment is pushing up aggregated investments, though some are choosing to postpone or even cancel investment projects owing to uncertainty related to profitability ahead. 
Capacity constraints and labour shortages:
 Indicators for both capacity constraints and labour shortages eased a bit further according to the network and remain below their historical averages. On aggregate, capacity constraints fell to 28% from 30%, implying slightly softer conditions. The decline was rather broad-based among sectors though most pronounced within oil services. The share reporting recruitment difficulties also eased to 17% from 18%. The service sector in particular reports of weaker competition from labour among consultants. There are large regional differences in the labour market. The South-West region has the largest recruitment difficulties, while only a few contacts report labour shortages in East and Central regions. Overall, the indicators point to some slack in the economy, which supports Norges Bank’s assessment that capacity utilization is drifting lower, pointing to a negative output gap ahead.
Employment expectations:
 Contacts expect modest employment growth of 0.1% q/q in coming quarters
, unchanged from the previous report and in line with Norges Bank’s estimate.
There are large sector differences, with the oil service sector planning to reduce staff while defence-related contacts within manufacturing and services are reporting a sharp staffing increase. Spare capacity within retail and construction are resulting in unchanged employment. 
Wage growth expectations:
 Wage growth expectations were unchanged for 2026 at 4.5%, near the 4.4% norm and in line with Norges Bank’s estimate. Meanwhile, expectations for 2027 were lowered marginally (-0.1ppt) to 4.0%, aligning with Norges Bank’s estimate though being below social partners’ 3.8% estimate from the latest Inflation Expectations Survey. Some contacts highlighted the risk of high inflation contributing to keeping wage growth elevated.
Implications Norges Bank: 
The Regional Network Report sends somewhat softer signals without indicating any dramatic shift. The easing in capacity indicators combined with marginally lower wage growth expectations in 2027 aligns with Norges Bank’s assessment that the output gap is turning negative. This should be comforting for Norges Bank though we are not convinced that it is enough for the bank to argue for underlying inflation prospects having changed materially. Output growth remains stable at 0.3% q/q, core inflation is back around 3% y/y, while labour market signals remain steady. We still regard the upcoming Sep 24 rate decision a 50/50 call but are leaning towards a rate hike.
